claim: The reported 99.56% accuracy of Finistral-7B-LoRA on Financial PhraseBank sentences_allagree is driven by train/test contamination, because FPB is a constituent source inside FinGPT/fingpt-sentiment-train, the corpus the model was fine-tuned on.
evidence: DIRECT EMPIRICAL OVERLAP (the decisive evidence): I loaded both datasets via HuggingFace `datasets` and cross-matched. Of the 2,264 FPB sentences_allagree evaluation sentences, 1,703 (75.22%) appear VERBATIM in the 76,772 FinGPT/fingpt-sentiment-train `input` column (identical under both exact raw-string match and normalized lowercase/strip-punctuation/collapse-whitespace match; fuzzy Jaccard>=0.9 adds only 4 more, to 75.40%). Script used: /tmp/overlap_final.py.

LABEL-LEVEL MEMORIZATION: For 100% of the 1,703 matched sentences, FinGPT/fingpt-sentiment-train stores the IDENTICAL 3-class gold label (positive/neutral/negative) that FPB sentences_allagree uses. The model was therefore trained on the exact (sentence, label) pairs it is later scored on. Match rate is uniform across classes (positive 77.2%, neutral 74.6%, negative 74.6%), so this is broad inclusion of FPB, not class-balanced subsampling.

TRAINING SPLIT MECHANICS: Finistral_Sentiment_analyst.py line 30-33 loads FinGPT/fingpt-sentiment-train and does ONLY `train_test_split(test_size=0.05, seed=42)`; the 95% portion is the fine-tuning set. So ~1,618 of the 1,703 FPB-allagree sentences land directly in the fine-tuning data, then the paper evaluates on the FULL 2,264 — a textbook train-on-test setup. The 5% internal val split is unrelated to and does not exclude the FPB eval set.

DOCUMENTED SOURCE COMPOSITION: FinGPT/fingpt-sentiment-train aggregates four sentiment sources — Financial PhraseBank (FPB), FiQA-SA, Twitter Financial News Sentiment (TFNS), and News With GPT Instructions (NWGI). Confirmed via the AI4Finance FinNLP benchmark code (test_fiqa/test_tfns/test_nwgi) and the FinGPT replication writeup, which states for FPB: 'We use the same split as BloombergGPT... in our task, all data in the train part were used in finetuning, So our results are far better than Bloomberg's.' Sources: https://github.com/AI4Finance-Foundation/FinGPT ; https://huggingface.co/datasets/flwrlabs/fingpt-sentiment-train (provenance mirror, documents 76,772 rows from the FinGPT repo) ; FinGPT papers arXiv:2306.06031, 2310.04793, 2307.10485.

DATASET IDENTITY CHECK: takala/financial_phrasebank is the FPB corpus (4,840 sentences; sentences_allagree = 2,264; arxiv:1307.5336). The FinGPT inputs contain its signature formatting (Finnish-company financial news with spaced punctuation, e.g. 'The value of the order is USD 2.3 mn .', 'Financial terms were not disclosed .', 'Order intake grew by 40 % year-on-year ...'), confirmed in the dataset preview rows and the flwrlabs mirror.

MECHANISM IS INDEPENDENT OF PROMPT-TEMPLATE MISMATCH: Even though training uses an [INST]...[/INST] template and the eval notebooks use an Alpaca Instruction/Input/Answer template, near-perfect accuracy is the expected outcome of memorization once the model has seen 75%+ of the exact test sentences with their correct labels. The template difference and the broken/low baselines (sub-majority-class 13-23%, padding_side warnings, 8-bit-vs-NF4 confusion) are separate harness issues; they do not explain Finistral's 99.56%, and contamination alone suffices. The 561 unmatched FPB sentences (mostly a distinct FPB train/test split slice) are the only genuinely held-out portion.
caveats: Measured verbatim overlap is 75.2% (1,703/2,264), not 100%. The remaining ~24.6% (561 sentences) are not found in the FinGPT inputs — most likely because FinGPT incorporated a specific FPB train split ('same split as BloombergGPT') rather than the entire AllAgree file, or due to minor preprocessing differences. So 99.56% accuracy on the FULL 2,264 cannot be 100% memorization, but contamination of three-quarters of the eval set is more than enough to manufacture a near-perfect headline number; a clean evaluation must report accuracy on the disjoint remainder separately.

FPB AllAgree was loaded from the raw FinancialPhraseBank-v1.0/Sentences_AllAgree.txt (2,264 lines, latin-1, 'sentence@label'); this is the canonical sentences_allagree config. Exact row-for-row identity with the specific HF snapshot the authors used could differ by a handful of lines but not materially.

I did not execute the authors' actual fine-tuned adapter (Ayansk11/Finistral-7B_lora) end-to-end to reproduce 99.56%; the contamination is proven at the data level (overlapping inputs + identical gold labels + train-on-all split), which is the root cause regardless of the exact reproduced score.

The overlap analysis was run unauthenticated against current HF dataset versions; FinGPT/fingpt-sentiment-train (updated 20 Nov 2023) and takala/financial_phrasebank are stable, so version drift is not a concern.
recommended_action: Treat the 99.56% as invalid (contaminated) and require a decontaminated re-evaluation before any acceptance. Exact decontamination procedure: (1) Normalize both sides — lowercase, strip all punctuation, collapse internal/trailing whitespace (this is essential because FPB uses spaced punctuation like 'mn .'). (2) Remove from the 2,264 FPB allagree eval set every sentence whose normalized form appears in the 76,772 FinGPT training `input` values via (a) exact-match, (b) normalized-match, and (c) fuzzy near-duplicate match using token Jaccard or MinHash/LSH with threshold ~0.9. In this corpus that removes 1,707 sentences, leaving a FPB-disjoint remainder of ~557. (3) Re-run the SAME inference harness on that disjoint remainder and report accuracy/weighted-F1 there; expect a large drop toward realistic FinBERT/FinGPT-class numbers (~80-90%, not 99.6%). (4) Critically, also fix the eval harness independently of contamination: use the [INST]...[/INST] template that matches training, set tokenizer.padding_side='left' for decoder-only generation, drop the 8-bit/NF4 mislabeling, use max_new_tokens (not max_length with padding=True), and compare like-for-like Mistral backbones (v0.1 vs v0.1, not v0.2/unsloth). (5) Re-evaluate ALL baselines under their original published inference procedures and report per-baseline confusion matrices; the current sub-majority-class baseline scores (13-23%, below the 61.6% neutral majority rate) are harness artifacts, not model quality, and must not stand. (6) Validate on a TRULY held-out external set never present in fingpt-sentiment-train (e.g. FiQA-SA test held out, SemEval-2017 Task 5, or a fresh hand-labeled financial set) with multi-seed mean±std and a significance test. (7) In the paper, add an explicit data-contamination/overlap-analysis section reporting these overlap counts, and correct the Sec 3.3/4.1/4.2/Table-4 code-vs-text mismatches (prompt template, Unsloth-not-used, LoRA targets q_proj/v_proj only, dropout 0.05, trainable-param count). Without (1)-(7) the central result is unsupported.

claim: There is NO data leakage between FinGPT/fingpt-sentiment-train and the takala/financial_phrasebank sentences_allagree evaluation set; the reported 99.56% accuracy is a legitimate generalization result.
evidence: Direct empirical overlap measured on the actual datasets: I downloaded FinGPT/fingpt-sentiment-train (76,772 rows; 30,235 unique inputs) and the full takala FPB allagree set (2,264 rows = 1,584 train + 680 test from the gtfintechlab/financial_phrasebank_sentences_allagree parquet mirror; class dist neg=303, neu=1391/1386, pos=570 — matching the paper's confusion-matrix diagonal 301/1385/568, confirming it is the same eval set).

1,699 of the 2,259 unique FPB allagree eval sentences (75.2%) appear VERBATIM in the FinGPT training inputs. Exact string match, whitespace-normalized match, and alphanumeric-only (punctuation/space-stripped) match ALL return the identical 1,699 — so this is not a fuzzy artifact, the sentences are literally the same text.

Label leakage is total: in 100% of the 1,699 overlapping sentences, the FinGPT training output contains the exact FPB gold label (negative/neutral/positive). The model was trained on the precise input->answer pairs it was later 'tested' on.

Reproducing the training script's own dataset.train_test_split(test_size=0.05, seed=42): all 1,699 leaked eval sentences fall inside the 95% TRAINING partition, so they were actually used to update the LoRA weights (not held out).
Leakage is uniform across all three classes (negative 74.6%, neutral 74.5%, positive 77.2%), which explains the near-perfect, balanced confusion matrix rather than majority-class collapse.

FPB is built from LexisNexis financial news and is dominated by Nordic/Finnish-company sentences; the FinGPT 'news' subset contains these same sentences verbatim (e.g. 'Teollisuuden Voima Oyj', 'Suominen Flexible Packaging is cutting 48 jobs in its unit in Tampere', 'Kesko's loyal customer magazine Pirkka with 2,462,000 readers'), visible directly in the FinGPT dataset preview. A web claim that FPB is 'not part of' FinGPT-train is contradicted by the raw data.

The premise that 'LoRA on q/v only cannot memorize 76k sentences' does not save the claim: with 75% of the test set seen with correct labels during 4 epochs at lr 1e-4, the model does not need to memorize — it has the answers, and only ~25% of the eval is genuinely held out.
caveats: Strongest point FOR the no-leakage position (honest steelman): ~24.8% (560 sentences) of the eval set was never seen in any form in the FinGPT corpus, so some genuine generalization is being measured on that slice — the 99.56% is not 100% leakage.

The mismatch between training prompt template ([INST]...[/INST]) and eval template (Instruction/Input/Answer) means the model is not trivially regurgitating a memorized string format, which slightly complicates a pure-memorization story — but it does not remove the leakage, because the underlying input->label association was still trained on.

The leaked-label check used coarse {negative/neutral/positive} mapping; a small number of FinGPT rows use a 7-point scale (strong/moderately/mildly), but those did not affect the 1,699 coarse-label matches (all matched the gold label), so this does not weaken the finding.

I used the gtfintechlab parquet mirror of FPB allagree because the canonical takala loader is a script unsupported by datasets 4.x; the mirror's row count (2,264) and class distribution exactly match the paper's eval, so substitution risk is negligible.

Even setting leakage aside, the reported sub-majority-class baselines (13-23% vs 61.6% majority) independently indicate a broken eval harness (right-padding on decoder-only models, neutral-default parser), so the comparative gap is also inflated — but that is a separate issue from the leakage that inflates Finistral's own number.
recommended_action: Treat the 99.56% as a data-leakage artifact, not a generalization result; the no-leakage claim is refuted. Require the authors to (1) de-duplicate FinGPT-train against FPB allagree and re-evaluate only on the ~560 (24.8%) sentences never seen in training, reporting accuracy/F1 on that disjoint slice; (2) report the verbatim-overlap statistic (1,699/2,259 = 75.2%, 100% label-consistent) in the paper as Reviewer 1 point 3 and Reviewer 2 point 1 demand; (3) fix the baseline eval harness (set padding_side='left', remove the neutral-default parser bias, match each baseline's native inference template and Mistral backbone version) before any comparative claim; (4) add multi-seed runs with mean/std and an external held-out financial dataset (e.g., FiQA, Twitter Financial News test, or a leakage-free FPB split) to substantiate generalization.

claim: The low baseline scores (13-23% accuracy, below the 61.6% majority-class rate) are an artifact of a broken evaluation harness (right-padding, wrong generation cap, ignored quant config, single shared prompt, inconsistent base), not genuine model performance.
evidence: RIGHT-PADDING (HIGH impact, decisive): test_final2.ipynb output streams contain 566 occurrences of the exact warning 'A decoder-only architecture is being used, but right-padding was detected! For correct generation results, please set padding_side=left' for the Falcon/Llama-3/Bloom baselines. The harness in /Users/ayansk11/Desktop/FinistralAI_code/test_final.ipynb (evaluate_model, cell 6) and test_final2.ipynb (cell 5) builds the tokenizer with AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(...) and never sets padding_side='left', then calls tokenizer(prompts, padding=True) with batch_size=8. For a decoder-only causal LM, pad tokens are appended AFTER the prompt; generation then continues from a PAD position so every sequence except the single longest in each batch is conditioned on trailing pad tokens, corrupting the first and subsequent generated tokens. This alone destroys batched output for the three baselines that fired the warning.

WRONG GENERATION CAP (HIGH impact): the loop calls model.generate(**tokens, max_length=512) which caps TOTAL length (prompt+generation), not max_new_tokens. The notebook output also shows the companion warning 'max_length is ignored when padding=True and there is no truncation strategy'. FPB prompts are short (~30-60 tokens), so the model is allowed to ramble for ~450 new tokens. The Mistral-base row took 5h31m (70s/it) vs the trained Finistral at ~1.8 it/s — direct evidence the base/baseline models generate long rambling continuations instead of a single label token. FinGPT's own official eval (AI4Finance FinGPT_Benchmark/benchmarks/fpb.py) uses max_new_tokens=10 with greedy do_sample=False, the opposite of this harness.

IGNORED QUANT CONFIG (MEDIUM impact, definitively proven): I reproduced the notebook's exact BitsAndBytesConfig(load_in_8bit=True, bnb_8bit_compute_dtype=float16, bnb_8bit_use_double_quant=True, bnb_8bit_quant_type='nf4') against the installed transformers API. The class __init__ only accepts the bnb_4bit_* family (bnb_4bit_compute_dtype/bnb_4bit_quant_type/bnb_4bit_use_double_quant) plus load_in_8bit/load_in_4bit; the three bnb_8bit_* kwargs fall into **kwargs and are SILENTLY DROPPED. cfg.to_dict() shows none of them are present; the config resolves to plain int8 (llm.int8()) with load_in_4bit=False, bnb_4bit_quant_type='fp4' (default, unused), use_double_quant=False. So the intended NF4 double-quant never happens — it is plain int8. (Note: 8-bit and NF4 are mutually exclusive anyway since NF4 is a 4-bit type, matching paper Sec 4.1's impossible '8-bit NF4 format'.)

INCONSISTENT BASE (MEDIUM impact): test_final.ipynb cell 4 sets the 'Mistral-7B-Base' row to base='unsloth/mistral-7b-v0.2', while Finistral uses base='mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1'. Different Mistral versions (v0.2 vs v0.1) are compared as if the same backbone, so the 'base' row does not even share Finistral's backbone.

PARSER DEFAULTS TO NEUTRAL (amplifier): extract_sentiment() returns 'neu' whenever no sentiment word is found (cell 5). I reproduced this: garbled/rambling outputs and pad-junk both return 'neu'. Because neutral is the 61.6% majority class, a merely non-responsive model would still score ~0.616. The baselines scoring 13-23% are BELOW this neutral floor, proving the harness does not merely fail-silent to neutral — it emits actively WRONG non-neutral labels (from corrupted right-padded generation) often enough to push accuracy below the majority-class baseline. No functioning model produces sub-majority-class accuracy on FPB-allagree.

PUBLISHED-SCORE CROSS-CHECK (decisive): FinLoRA (arXiv:2505.19819, Table 4) reports LoRA/QLoRA-finetuned 7-8B models at ~84-86% accuracy / 0.91-0.92 weighted F1 on Financial PhraseBank, and even the UNtuned Llama-3.1-8B base at 68.73% — all far above both the 13-23% reported here and the 61.6% majority floor. WebSearch corroborates FinGPT-family FPB results of ~0.88 accuracy / 0.84 F1. The reported baselines are 4-6x below published values for the identical adapters, which is only explainable by a broken harness, not by genuine model quality.

PAPER vs CODE corroboration: the paper's own text matches the broken config and contradicts the training code, confirming the authors transcribed the buggy harness rather than a corrected run. tex line 281 'load the backbone in 8-bit NF4 format (load_in_8bit=True)'; line 285 LoRA into 'every attention-projection and feed-forward linear layer' (code targets only q_proj,v_proj); line 297 LoRA dropout 0.10 (code 0.05); abstract val loss 0.1008 vs Table 6 0.1009; full-precision adapter 83.9MB but 4-bit GGML 168MB (a 4-bit variant larger than fp16 is implausible).
caveats: I could not execute the full GPU evaluation (no model weights / GPU / gated-repo access in this environment), so the causal link from each bug to each exact numeric score is established by mechanism + the recorded warnings + published-score comparison, not by a from-scratch re-run. A definitive fix-and-rerun (set padding_side='left', use max_new_tokens=8-10, apply each adapter's official prompt, consistent base) is the recommended confirmation.

The Finistral row itself is NOT directly invalidated by the right-padding bug the way the baselines are: because Finistral was trained to emit the label token immediately, its short greedy output is comparatively robust to the corruption (it ran at ~1.8 it/s, not 70s/it). However its 99.56% is still suspect for separate reasons outside this task's scope: possible FinGPT-train/FPB data leakage (FPB-derived sentences may appear in the FinGPT training corpus) and single-run/no-seed evaluation — these are Reviewer 1 pts 1,3,5 and Reviewer 2 pts 1,2,5 and are not resolved here.

FinGPT's exact documented prompt could not be quoted verbatim from the model card (it links out to a GitHub inference notebook); the template details come from the AI4Finance FinGPT_Benchmark eval code and the model card structure, which is sufficient to show the harness prompt differs (missing Options line, 3-way vs trained 2-way) but the precise per-adapter expected string should be cited from the repo when rebutting.

The bnb int8 fallback (vs intended NF4) is the lowest-impact of the bugs: plain int8 inference is itself reasonably accurate, so it mildly degrades rather than breaks the baselines. It is strong evidence of harness carelessness and a direct paper/code contradiction, but right-padding + max_length + prompt mismatch are the dominant causes of the sub-majority scores.
recommended_action: Treat the 13-23% baseline scores as an evaluation-harness artifact and do not present them as evidence of Finistral's superiority. To rebut Reviewer 1 (pts 1,2) and Reviewer 2 (pts 2,3,4): re-run all baselines with a corrected harness — (a) AutoTokenizer(..., padding_side='left') for every decoder-only model; (b) generate(max_new_tokens=8) instead of max_length=512; (c) each FinGPT-mt adapter evaluated with its OWN official FinGPT inference prompt (Instruction/Input/Answer + 'Options:' line) per AI4Finance FinGPT_Benchmark, not one shared Alpaca prompt; (d) a single consistent base (e.g. compare against mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1, not unsloth/mistral-7b-v0.2); (e) fix BitsAndBytesConfig to either valid load_in_8bit (drop the bnb_8bit_* kwargs) or genuine load_in_4bit + bnb_4bit_quant_type='nf4' + bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=True. Expect corrected FinGPT baselines to land near published ~0.8-0.86 accuracy / ~0.84-0.92 F1, which will simultaneously shrink Finistral's apparent margin and remove the 'baselines below majority class' red flag. Separately, the authors must also reconcile the paper's Sec 4.1/4.2 and Table 4/6 claims with Finistral_Sentiment_analyst.py (q_proj/v_proj only, dropout 0.05, [INST] template, no Unsloth, no quantization in training) and address the unresolved Finistral-side issues (data-leakage dedup, multi-seed mean+/-std) before the 99.56% can be trusted.

claim: The manuscript finistral_grjournals.tex contains numerous factual inconsistencies with the actual training script (Finistral_Sentiment_analyst.py) and evaluation notebooks (test_final.ipynb, test_final2.ipynb, inference_test.ipynb).
evidence: [1] UNSLOTH NEVER USED. Manuscript Sec 4.1 (Base Model, lines 281, 610-611): 'We utilise Unsloth, an open-source framework that applies custom Triton kernels to accelerate LoRA fine-tuning by up to 2x while reducing VRAM consumption by approximately 70%', with citation \cite{unsloth2023}. CODE REALITY: Finistral_Sentiment_analyst.py imports nothing from unsloth; it uses plain transformers AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained + peft.get_peft_model + HF Trainer. The string 'unsloth' appears in code only as the EVAL baseline base model 'unsloth/mistral-7b-v0.2' (test_final.ipynb), not in training. WHY IT MATTERS: fabricated tooling/citation misrepresents the method and reproducibility claims; the cited speed/VRAM benefits were never realized. FIX (text): delete all Unsloth claims and the \cite{unsloth2023} reference; describe the actual stack (transformers + peft + HF Trainer + gradient checkpointing + xformers).

[2] QUANTIZATION NOT USED IN TRAINING + IMPOSSIBLE '8-bit NF4'. Manuscript Sec 4.1 (line 281): 'We load the backbone in 8-bit NF4 format (load_in_8bit=True in Transformers) so that a single 40 GB A100 can accommodate both weights and optimiser states.' CODE REALITY: training loads in NO quantization at all -- AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(base_model, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16) with no BitsAndBytesConfig and no load_in_8bit. Additionally '8-bit NF4' is self-contradictory: NF4 (NormalFloat4) is a 4-bit dtype; load_in_8bit and NF4 are mutually exclusive and cannot coexist. WHY IT MATTERS: the central memory/efficiency claim describes a configuration that does not exist and is technically impossible; it conflates the eval-time 8-bit loading with training. FIX (text): state training used bf16 full-precision weights (no quantization); remove the impossible '8-bit NF4' phrase. (Note: load_in_8bit=True actually appears only in the EVAL notebooks, where it is paired with a self-contradictory bnb_8bit_quant_type='nf4' that bitsandbytes ignores for 8-bit.)

[3] LoRA TARGET MODULES: 'every attention + FFN layer' vs q_proj/v_proj only. Manuscript Sec 4.2 (line 285): LoRA injected 'into every attention-projection and feed-forward linear layer.' CODE REALITY: LoraConfig(target_modules=['q_proj','v_proj']) -- only the query and value attention projections; NOT k_proj, o_proj, and NOT any FFN/MLP layers (gate_proj, up_proj, down_proj). WHY IT MATTERS: directly contradicts the param-count claims and overstates adapter coverage; a reviewer reproducing 'all layers' would get a different (larger) adapter. FIX (text): correct to 'LoRA applied to the q_proj and v_proj attention projections only.'

[4] LoRA DROPOUT: paper 0.10 vs code 0.05. Manuscript Table 4 (LoRA Hyperparameters, line 297): 'LoRA dropout 0.10'. CODE REALITY: LoraConfig(lora_dropout=0.05). WHY IT MATTERS: a stated hyperparameter is wrong by 2x; undermines reproducibility of the exact recipe. FIX (text): change Table 4 to 0.05 (or rerun with 0.10 if that value is intended, but code is authoritative).

[5] TRAINABLE PARAMETER COUNT/PERCENT overstated ~33%. Manuscript Table 4 + abstract + novelty (lines 125, 149, 179, 298, 488): 'Trainable parameters approx 9M (0.2% of 7B)'. CODE REALITY: with r=16 on q_proj (4096->4096) and v_proj (4096->1024, GQA) across 32 layers, trainable params = 16*(4096+4096)*32 + 16*(4096+1024)*32 = 6,815,744 approx 6.82M = approx 0.094% of 7.24B, NOT 9M/0.2%. The 9M/0.2% figure would only be plausible if LoRA targeted more modules (consistent with the false 'all layers' claim in item 3) -- the two errors are linked. WHY IT MATTERS: headline novelty/efficiency numbers (0.2%) are inflated ~2x; the real number (~0.094%) is actually a stronger efficiency claim, so the error is gratuitous. FIX (text): report the actual count from model.print_trainable_parameters() (~6.8M, ~0.094%); reconcile with the corrected target_modules.

[6] ADAPTER FILE SIZES IMPLAUSIBLE: 4-bit GGML (168MB) LARGER than fp16 (83.9MB). Manuscript abstract, Sec 1 Contributions, Sec 4.2 (lines 125, 185, 299, 304): full-precision adapter = 83.9MB; '4-bit GGML variant' / ggml-adapter-model.bin = 168MB. CODE REALITY: no code produces or exports a GGML/4-bit adapter (the training script only does model.push_to_hub; no llama.cpp/GGML conversion exists in any file). Physically, a 4-bit quantized variant of the same weights cannot be ~2x LARGER than the fp16 version; the 168MB > 83.9MB relationship is internally impossible. WHY IT MATTERS: the 4-bit/CPU-deployment and '<100ms CPU (4-bit GGML)' claims (Sec 5.4, line 500) rest on an artifact that appears not to exist and whose stated size is self-contradictory. FIX: either produce and correctly measure a real 4-bit adapter (which would be SMALLER, roughly 20-25MB), or remove all GGML/4-bit/CPU-latency claims and the '4-bit GGML weights' release claim.

[7] PROMPT TEMPLATE MISDESCRIBED + TRAIN/EVAL MISMATCH. Manuscript Sec 3.3 (lines 241-251): claims each sentence is 'wrapped exactly as in the training script' using the Alpaca-style 'Instruction: ... Input: {text} Answer:' format. CODE REALITY: the TRAINING script (Finistral_Sentiment_analyst.py, line 96) uses a DIFFERENT Mistral chat template: prompt = f'[INST]{inp}\n{instr} [/INST]', full = prompt + ' ' + out. The 'Instruction/Input/Answer' format is what the EVAL notebooks use (make_prompt in test_final*.ipynb), NOT the training script. So (a) the paper's description of the training template is factually wrong, and (b) there is a genuine train-vs-eval prompt-format mismatch: the model was trained on [INST]...[/INST] but evaluated with Alpaca-style prompts. WHY IT MATTERS: 'wrapped exactly as in the training script' is false; the mismatch is a real methodological confound (a model that scores 99.56% under a different prompt than it was trained on warrants scrutiny). FIX (text): show the true [INST] training template; explicitly disclose and justify the eval prompt difference, or rerun eval with the [INST] template for consistency.

[8] VALIDATION-LOSS VALUE INCONSISTENT WITHIN PAPER: 0.1008 vs 0.1009. Manuscript abstract is absent of the value but Sec 1.2 (line 179), Sec 4.3 (line 334), and Sec 6.2 (line 476) state best val loss = 0.1008 'after epoch 2', while Table 6 (Validation-loss Trajectory, line 345) lists epoch-2 validation loss = 0.1009 (bolded as best). The two numbers disagree. WHY IT MATTERS: an internal numeric inconsistency in the headline training result; trivially fixable but signals loose bookkeeping. FIX (text): pick the value from the actual training logs and use it consistently in all four locations.

[9] BASELINE EVAL NOT 'IDENTICAL TRUNCATION + GREEDY DECODING'. Manuscript Sec 5.1 (line 379): 'All baselines are evaluated with the same instruction prompt, identical truncation rules, and greedy decoding.' CODE REALITY (test_final*.ipynb evaluate_model): (a) generation is model.generate(**tokens, max_length=512) with NO do_sample/num_beams set and NO max_new_tokens -- it relies on defaults and emits 'max_length is ignored when padding=True and there is no truncation strategy'; greedy is the default but is never explicitly set, and because max_length==tokenizer max_length==512 with padded inputs, generation frequently produces zero or few new tokens. (b) tokenizer uses padding=True with DEFAULT right padding; the notebook output shows 'A decoder-only architecture is being used, but right-padding was detected! please set padding_side=left' for the baselines (Falcon/Llama-3/Bloom), which corrupts decoder-only generation. (c) extract_sentiment() defaults to 'neu' when no sentiment word is found, so broken generations are silently scored as neutral. WHY IT MATTERS: the baselines were NOT evaluated under a correct, identical, greedy protocol; right-padding + max_length collision + neutral-default parser is a broken harness, which fully explains why all FinGPT baselines score 13-23% -- BELOW the 61.6% majority-class (neutral) rate. The paper's claim of a fair identical protocol is false; the 'state-of-the-art, +78 F1' comparison is invalid. FIX (code+rerun): set padding_side='left', use max_new_tokens (e.g. 5-10) instead of max_length, evaluate each baseline with its own correct prompt/inference procedure, and re-report; the corrected baselines will be far higher and the headline margins will shrink dramatically.

[10] MISMATCHED MISTRAL BACKBONE FOR THE 'BASE' BASELINE. Manuscript Table 5 + Sec 5 present 'Mistral-7B-Base' as the zero-shot backbone of Finistral. CODE REALITY: test_final.ipynb sets Mistral-7B-Base base='unsloth/mistral-7b-v0.2' while Finistral uses base='mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1'. These are DIFFERENT model versions (v0.2 vs v0.1) from different uploaders, compared as if the same backbone. WHY IT MATTERS: the headline '+69-70 F1 over the Mistral-7B backbone' compares the adapter against a different base model than it was actually built on, invalidating the 'gain over backbone' attribution.
